**Step 1: Lock down non-location permissions.** Go through Settings > Privacy and systematically review Microphone, Camera, Photos, Contacts, and Calendar access. **Step 4: Review third-party sign-ins.** Go to Settings > [Your Name] > Password & Security (iPhone) or Google Account > Security (Android) and remove old app permissions you no longer use. Apps that can sign in as you often retain broad data access long after you've stopped using them.

These changes won't break your everyday workflow since you're already selective about which apps get location access.

**Months 1–6: Foundation & Assessment**
- Get your credit report and score; aim for 740+ if possible (better rates)

- Build your emergency fund to 3–6 months of expenses (~$13k–$26k) if you haven't already
- Start tracking your savings rate; aim to save aggressively toward the down payment

**Months 7–12: Aggressive Saving & Optimization**
- Lock in a monthly savings target (ideally 15–20% of gross income if possible)
- Review your budget with fresh eyes—cut discretionary spending where you can without burning out
- Consider a side income boost if feasible (freelance work, part-time gig)
- Research first-time homebuyer programs in your area; some offer down-payment assistance or better rates
- Continue building credit and paying down any high-interest debt

**Months 13–18: Down Payment Target & Mortgage Prep**
- Aim to have 10–15% down saved ($52k–$78k) by this point
- Get a second pre-qualification to see if your financial position has improved your rate offer
- Start researching neighborhoods and getting a sense of actual market prices
- Review your tax situation with an accountant; understand what deductions you might claim as a homeowner

**Months 19–24: Final Push & Ready to Move**
- Reach your target down payment (ideally 15–20% if possible, to avoid PMI)
- Get a final pre-approval letter
- Start seriously house hunting; get a real estate agent if helpful
- Have your finances audit-ready: tax returns, pay stubs, bank statements organized
- Plan for closing costs (~3–5% of loan amount, or $14k–$23k in your case)
